Ramp builds software that moves real money, from bill payments and corporate cards to reimbursements, accounting integrations, and travel. Our customers rely on us to keep their operations running: invoices get paid, books get closed, and finance leaders can trust the data behind every decision.

In this role, you will be the person who spots where customers are getting stuck and drives issues to a clear resolution. You will learn a complex product deeply enough to troubleshoot across payments, bank linking, accounting syncs, and card programs, then partner with teams across Engineering, Risk, Product, and Partnerships to get problems solved. - Be the voice of Ramp's Customer Support. You'll spend your day engaging with customers, primarily via live calls, email, and chat.

- Diagnose across a broad product surface. Ramp isn't one product — it's payments, cards, travel, accounting integrations, and more. You'll need to understand how they connect and where they break.

- Operate with an ownership mindset, managing escalations end-to-end. You take full accountability for every ticket you handle. When an issue crosses team boundaries — risk, engineering, product, partnerships — you route it correctly, follow up, and make sure the customer isn't left waiting. - Communicate with precision and empathy. Our customers are financially sophisticated. You need to explain what's happening, what you're doing about it, and what they should expect — clearly and without filler.

- You're a systems thinker: you don't just solve the ticket in front of you, you ask why the problem exists and how to prevent it from happening again.

- You actively use AI tools — Claude, Notion AI, research and workflow tools — and can demonstrate how you've applied them to get real work done. This is a hard requirement.

- You're fast-moving while holding yourself to a high bar for execution: you balance speed, accuracy, and thoroughness in every interaction.

- You can hold a technical conversation about how systems connect (APIs, bank integrations, accounting software) even if you're not writing code.

- You manage competing priorities without dropping things. When you have 15 open issues across 4 internal teams, nothing falls through.

- You're comfortable on the phone. Many interactions start there.

- You have a demonstrated track record of exceeding key performance standards, including CSAT, QA, and speed-of-service metrics.

- Experience building workflows or automations using AI tools, not just prompting

- Familiarity with accounting workflows (AP/AR, GL, reconciliation) or ERP integrations (NetSuite, QuickBooks, Sage)

- Background in payments infrastructure (ACH, wire transfers, card networks)

- Track record of working somewhere that shipped product fast and expected CX to keep up

About MorphLabs

MorphLabs is building non-invasive telekinesis: a brain interface that turns movement intent into action, starting with people underserved by existing technology.

We are starting with continuous, intuitive prosthetic control for upper-limb amputees, decoding movement intent from EEG in real time, without surgery or reliance on muscle sensors. We develop the hardware and models together, treating signal quality, learning and control as one problem. Prosthetics are where we start, not where we stop.

We are a small, scrappy, high-throughput team in NYC. We have raised a substantial pre-seed round, with our seed round underway, and we move quickly between research and building.

The role

The central problem at MorphLabs is learning a mapping from EEG to intended movement that holds up across people and over time. Those models drive prosthetic and robotic hands, on-screen cursors and more.

As a Research Intern, you'll spend five months on one well-scoped research project at the center of that problem. You'll work directly with our CTO and the founding team, own your project from the first question to the result, and be expected to ship something real: a decoder running in our system, a benchmark we adopt, or a clear finding that changes what we try next.

This is not a side project. Interns work on the same data, hardware and open problems as the rest of the team.

What you'll do

- Transfer learning across subjects, sessions and devices. Help build decoders that adapt to new users from minimal calibration data and stay robust to drift between sessions and headsets.

- Self-supervised pretraining. Try pretraining objectives on our growing, largely unlabeled EEG corpus, and measure how well they transfer to real control.

- Online closed-loop decoding. Help move models from offline benchmarks to causal, low-latency decoders, and look into why offline accuracy doesn't always predict online performance.

- Paradigm design. Help design the tasks and data-collection protocols that produce informative training data, and use each result to shape the next experiment.

- Evaluation and benchmarking. Contribute to the metrics, held-out splits and benchmarks we use to judge decoders, offline and online.

- Inform the hardware. Share what the models reveal about signal quality with our hardware team, and help validate our custom headset against third-party systems.

- Ship what works. Turn promising results into reproducible decoders running in our system, and write up what worked and what didn't.

What you'll have

- Data, every day. We record new EEG daily, and our corpus already spans thousands of hours.

- Our own hardware. We build our own headset, electrodes and amplifier, and also work with data from third-party headsets.

- An IRB already in place, covering both healthy participants and patients.

- The resources to do the work. Compute and equipment won't be the bottleneck.

Who we're looking for

We're looking for students and early-career researchers (undergraduate, master's or PhD) who have already built things. What you've done matters more than your year, school or degree. You don't need a background in neuroscience or BCI; strong researchers can pick up the domain.

You may be a good fit if you have:

- Research you can point to, such as papers, reports or code, and a clear account of what you did yourself

- Models you built and trained yourself on noisy time series (speech, audio, sensors, robotics and neural data all count), and can explain your architecture and objective choices and how you debugged training and generalization

- Models that kept working when the data shifted, across people, sessions, devices or environments, and an understanding of why

- Rigorous, reproducible work: fair baselines, ablation studies, test sets that hold out whole sessions or people, and results others can reproduce

- Math and statistics you actually use in modeling decisions: probability, optimization, linear algebra and uncertainty

- An experiment or task you designed that produced useful data, or human-subjects research, including under IRB-approved protocols

- The ability to run experiments quickly and let each result sharpen the next one, while working independently and writing clearly

Strong candidates may also have:

- A background in dynamical systems, geometry or information theory that shapes how you think about representations, time structure or model design

- Experience with biosignals, neural data or non-invasive BCIs

- Experience with real-time or closed-loop systems, where latency matters and offline accuracy isn't the whole story

- Experience learning from limited data: self-supervision, and choosing the next experiment when data is scarce

- Pretraining experience where the results carried over to a downstream task

- First-author papers or other substantial research results. Quality matters more than venue.

These are guidelines, not a checklist. Exceptional researchers often come from unconventional backgrounds, so apply even if you're not an exact fit.

Job Description:

Job Family Definition

Students or recent graduates of a college, university, or other accredited academic program who are pursuing or have recently completed a degree in a relevant technical field. Supports technical projects aligned with their area of study, including research, testing, troubleshooting, collaboration, problem-solving, and creative thinking. Role Summary

HPE Networking is seeking a motivated student to join a cross-functional engineering team developing next-generation wireless access points. This hands-on internship provides experience in product integration, hardware bring-up, design validation, compliance testing, troubleshooting, laboratory measurements, and factory yield analysis.

The intern will collaborate with engineers across RF, power, digital, systems, manufacturing, and product development disciplines while contributing to an active wireless networking project.

Responsibilities

- Support senior engineers with assigned technical projects involving wireless access point hardware development and product integration.
- Assist with the bring-up, integration, and validation of wireless access points.
- Perform testing against design specifications, including Design Validation Testing (DVT).
- Support conformance and electrical compliance testing, including:
- Help identify, troubleshoot, and document hardware and system-level issues.
- Support factory yield analysis by reviewing test data, identifying trends, and helping investigate opportunities for improvement.
- Assist with laboratory testing using equipment such as: Spectrum analyzers, Network analyzers, Oscilloscopes, Power meters, Current-measurement equipment, Other applicable RF, power, and electronic test equipment
- Develop practical knowledge of wireless and networking protocols at the physical and system levels, including Wi-Fi and next-generation wireless technologies, including IEEE 802.11bn/Wi-Fi 8, Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE), Zigbee, Ultra-Wideband (UWB), Power over Ethernet (PoE), including IEEE 802.3, Ethernet
- Assist with maintaining, updating, and documenting hardware, test setups, software tools, and technical systems.
- Use data-analysis and AI-assisted tools, where appropriate, to analyze test results and support engineering activities.
- Collaborate with engineers across RF, power, digital, systems, manufacturing, and product development disciplines.
- Participate in team meetings, technical reviews, project discussions, and other team activities.
- Learn and apply engineering methodologies, laboratory procedures, and product development processes.
- Complete assigned tasks accurately and efficiently while meeting project deadlines.
- Participate in periodic reviews to provide project updates, receive feedback, and incorporate guidance into assigned work.
- Follow applicable safety procedures when working with electronic equipment, RF systems, power supplies, surge testing, and HIPOT testing.

Education and Experience

- Currently pursuing a bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Electrical and Computer Engineering, or a related technical field.
- Familiarity with technical tools, laboratory equipment, programming, scripting, or data-analysis methods is preferred.

Knowledge and Skills

- Strong interest in wireless hardware, networking, electronic systems, and product development.

- Basic understanding of electrical engineering principles and electronic circuits.
- Interest or foundational knowledge in one or more of the following areas: RF and microwave systems, Power over Ethernet, power regulation, or power conversion, Digital logic, processors, memories, and interfaces, Signal integrity and hardware validation
- Basic programming or scripting knowledge, such as Python, MATLAB, or a similar language.
- Ability to collect, analyze, and communicate technical data.
- Strong problem-solving, troubleshooting, and analytical skills.
- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
- Ability to collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams.
- Strong attention to detail and commitment to accurate documentation.
- Effective time-management skills and the ability to work with project deadlines.
- A collaborative, solution-focused mindset and willingness to learn.
- Ability to work safely and follow established laboratory and engineering procedures.

About Mercor

Mercor’s mission is to organize human intelligence for the AI economy. We build the infrastructure that enables frontier AI labs and enterprises to train, evaluate, and improve AI on real-world professional work. More than five million experts have joined our network, and we pay out over $5 million daily for their knowledge and expertise.

We built our training and evaluation infrastructure alongside the world’s leading AI labs. Now, we’re bringing those capabilities to enterprises across industries, enabling them to train, evaluate, and improve AI using their own expertise and standards. Our APEX benchmarks measure how AI performs on economically valuable work, while our enterprise evaluations and post-training capabilities turn those insights into measurable improvements across real-world workflows.

Our work sits at the intersection of frontier AI, human expertise, and real-world application. We’re solving problems few companies have encountered, with the opportunity to influence what the world’s most advanced AI systems become capable of doing. We’re looking for people who bring different perspectives, take ownership, exercise sound judgment, and hold themselves to an exceptionally high standard. You’ll have the opportunity to do consequential work alongside talented colleagues who challenge one another, collaborate openly, and share a commitment to excellence.

Mercor is profitable and recently raised a $750 million Series D at a $20 billion valuation. We work in person five days a week in San Francisco, New York, and London.

About the Role

As a Research Engineer at Mercor, you’ll work at the intersection of engineering and applied AI research. You’ll own benchmarking pipelines, evaluation systems, and failure analysis workflows that directly inform how we train and improve frontier language models.
Your work will define how we measure tool use, agentic behavior, and real-world reasoning. You’ll design and run evals, build rubrics and scorers, and turn failure analysis into actionable improvements for post-training, RLVR, and data pipelines.

What You’ll Do

- Benchmarking: Design, implement, and maintain benchmarks and metrics for tool use, agentic behavior, and real-world reasoning; ensure benchmarks scale with training and stay aligned with product and research goals.

- Evaluation systems: Build and operate LLM evaluation systems end-to-end runs, scoring, dashboards, and reporting, so researchers and applied AI teams can track model performance and compare runs at scale.

- Failure analysis: Run systematic failure analysis on model outputs (e.g., wrong tool use, reasoning errors, safety/alignment issues); categorize failure modes, quantify prevalence, and feed findings into reward design, data curation, and benchmark design.

- Rubrics and evaluators: Create and refine rubrics, automated evaluators, and scoring frameworks that drive training and evaluation decisions; balance rigor with scalability (human vs. model-as-judge, calibration, agreement).

- Data quality and usability: Quantify data usability, quality, and impact on key benchmarks; use evals and failure analysis to guide data generation, augmentation, and curation.

- Cross-team collaboration: Work with AI researchers, applied AI teams, and data producers to align evals with training objectives and to prioritize benchmarks and failure analyses that matter most.

- Ownership in a fast-paced environment: Operate in a high-iteration research setting with strong ownership of benchmarks, evals, and failure-analysis workflows.

What We’re Looking For

- Strong applied research background, with focus on model evaluation, benchmarking, and/or failure analysis.

- Strong coding skills and hands-on experience with ML models and evaluation code.

- Solid grasp of data structures, algorithms, and backend systems.

- Comfort with APIs, SQL/NoSQL, and cloud platforms for running and storing eval results.

- Ability to reason about model behavior, experimental results, and data quality from evals and failure analyses.

- Excitement to work in person in San Francisco five days a week in a high-intensity, high-ownership environment.

Nice To Have
